title: National Commissioners Invitational Tournament
source:

The '''National Commissioners Invitational Tournament''' was an eight-team postseason men's [[college basketball]] tournament run by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA). It was introduced in 1974 as the '''Collegiate Commissioners Association Tournament'''. Invitees were runner-up teams in major conferences, which were required to participate, creating a threat to the established [[National Invitation Tournament]] (NIT),<ref name=tolliver>{{cite book|last=Tolliver|first=Melanie|title=Indiana University Basketball: For the Thrill of It!|date=2002|publisher=Sports Publishing L.L.C.|isbn=978-1-58261-579-0|page=31|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Yj_G7-ZILNgC&pg=PA28}}</ref> which, at that time, the NCAA did not control.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2136724|title=NCAA Buys Tournaments, Ends NIT Litigation|website= ESPN|last=Katz|first=Andy|date=August 17, 2005|access-date=March 19, 2025}}</ref> [[Bobby Knight]], head coach of [[1973–74 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]], winner of the inaugural tournament, did not want to participate, because he believed it was created to "run the NIT out of business," which he opposed.<ref name=tolliver/> The tournament lasted only two years before being discontinued after changes to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] rules, which allowed more than one team per conference to participate.

== Summary ==
The tournament was won in 1974 by [[1973–74 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] over [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], 85–60, in [[St. Louis, Missouri]]. The [[1974 Collegiate Commissioners Association Tournament|1974 tournament]] featured a collection of teams that came in second in their conferences due to NCAA tournament rules at the time which only invited conference champions.

In 1975, the [[1975 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] expanded to include at-large teams, from a total of 25 to 32 teams and began inviting more than one team from some conferences rather than solely conference champions. However, the [[1975 National Commissioners Invitational Tournament|1975 tournament]], renamed the ''National Commissioners Invitational Tournament'', was still held and was won by [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake]] over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], 83–76, in [[Louisville, Kentucky]].

The Commissioners Invitational Tournament was discontinued after the 1975 tournament.
